summary: @servicetitan/grid ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper executing 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) that, on every `npm install`, detects the host platform and libc, downloads a Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` containing a large string/numeric dictionary array and a rotating-array unpacker (`WV8StW`) — its behavior is not readable statically. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling bundle at install time bypasses Node-based static analysis and guarantees the opaque payload runs against the installer on install. The install-time dropper is inconsistent with the package's stated purpose (a React/Kendo grid UI component), and `dist/` ships legitimate-looking grid wrappers that serve as cover for the hostile preinstall path. The `@servicetitan` scope suggests impersonation of the corporate namespace to trojanize dependency graphs pulling in what appears to be an internal component.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
